title: False Positives, Inaccurate, Annoying, Worthless. AVOID at all Costs!
body: I've had this app for months and multiple updates and I am truly pretty disgusted by it. Living in Alaska I was hoping to have a better app that would actually be useful and I've reverted back to old Aurora Fcst app in conduction with referencing twitter and websites. The app will say the forecast is 2 but then my phone starts going nuts and alerting every couple of minutes saying it is a 7, or an 8, or a 10 in the northern hemisphere. I look outside and not even a light hint of aurora. I'm also trying to figure out how or why I'm getting bombarded with 7-10 level alerts when the forecast for the day is 1 or 2 and this happening all day long. I then login and check multiple other online resources and there are no alerts, no storms, no heightened activity and no aurora being reported anywhere or anything forthcoming. One of the worst parts is that it will alert over and over and over again with these false positives sometimes only 2 or 3 minutes a apart sometimes. Also don't trust that it has sync'd up when it says it has sync'd your alert level as it seems to occasionally randomly revert back. The only way to truly get it to sync is to shut off alerting completing and turn it back on at the new level. On top of it being a next to worthless for anything other than maybe the forecast which it gets from the geophysical institute I believe, I don't appreciate the ads (even when i have done the $1.99 upgrade) and a whole section of the app to market aurora tours. Save the space on your phone and don't install this application, and for goodness sake don't spend $1.99 on the alerting upgrade. You will be regretting it probably minutes later.

title: Could Use Improvements
body: The Push Notifications are too much. I currently have it set at 9 of 10 and I get alerts constantly. I'd say I get at least 15-20 alerts every day. I'd like to be notified when there is a significant auroral event, not multiple times every day. Where I live, the Northern Lights are only visible occasionally, so seeing such high numbers every single night essentially renders them meaningless to me. Also, I receive daytime alerts. There should, at the very least, be an option to turn alerts off during the day without having to switch the Push Notifications on and off every night. The app already knows my location and displays it on a map. Maybe, in the future, this could become more integrated into the app. I do like that it also lists the daily forecast using UAF data. I find I usually have more success using that to predict my chances of seeing the lights on any given night than if I just go by the NOAA POES data alone. This app looks great and shows promise, but it needs to improve its practicality. Like I said, tweaking the Push Notifications to exclude alerts during daylight and twilight hours based on current location would dramatically improve its usefulness.

It saved me from staying up all night the following night bc I could see that the aurora never made it lower than the Hudson Bay while it was dark near me so I just put the camera out and went to sleep!! You never know when these storms will hit but having juuuuust a little more info about it than the average person is definitely worth the download and dang it I wish I upgraded during the 5/2024 event…. Oh well I hope I’m alive the next time we get a G5 solar storm AND THAT ITS CLEAR but if I am ill have this app handy! It was fun to see 3% chance for aurora in your area and it was right!! Couldn’t see with the naked eye but the time lapse video will be burned into my memory forever! And if I ever decide to travel and see the lights I would ABSOLUTELY upgrade and pay for the service. I never review apps but felt I wanted to thank the developers of this app bc I really had a lot of use for it bc of the weather in my area!! Thank you!!
